Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.4% today to $457.22, continuing a downward slide from a peak of $478 just a week ago. The immediate trigger is oil prices sliding over 2% today as traders weigh whether threats to Saudi energy infrastructure will actually materialize into supply disruptions or simply destroy demand through higher prices—a real tension that leaves refiners uncertain. When oil gets too expensive, consumers and businesses pull back on consumption, which hurts refiner margins even if crude supplies remain plentiful.

The broader pattern here reflects the volatility baked into the current moment: crude has swung between $107–$115 per barrel over the past few days as Middle East tensions flare and ease. Refineries are running near full capacity (93.4%), which is normally good for throughput, but if demand truly weakens from high prices, utilization rates could fall and squeeze margins tighter. The stock's decline mirrors the market's shift from geopolitical panic-buying oil to worry about demand destruction—a headwind for refiners that needs actual consumption recovery to reverse.
